'''David Phillips''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|commas=on|CBE|FRSC|FRS}} (born 3 December 1939)<ref name=whoswho/> is a British chemist specialising in [[photochemistry]] and lasers, and was president of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] from 2010 to 2012.<ref name=RSC>[http://www.rsc.org/AboutUs/Governance/president.asp www.rsc.org RSC President]</ref>

==Education and early life==
Phillips was born 3 December 1939 in Kendal, lived in South Shields and attended the Grammar School.<ref name=RSC/><ref name=whoswho/> He studied at the [[University of Birmingham]] attaining a BSc and PhD.<ref name=whoswho/>

==Career and research==
Phillips began his career doing [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] and the [[Academy of Sciences of the USSR]].<ref name=RSC/><ref name=Desert>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b010t31j Desert Island Discs] Professor David Phillips</ref> He was appointed a lecturer in chemistry at the [[University of Southampton]], rising to the status of [[Reader (academic rank)|Reader]] then becoming Wolfson Professor of [[Natural Philosophy]], at the [[Royal Institution]]. In 1981, Phillips became a founding member of the [[World Cultural Council]].<ref>{{cite web | title = About Us | publisher = [[World Cultural Council]] | url = http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/about-us/ | access-date=2016-11-08}}</ref> In 1989 he moved to [[Imperial College]], London as professor of [[physical chemistry]] and held a number of senior posts there.<ref name=RSC/> Once when he took the lift in the Chemistry Department, it stopped on every floor. When he got out he said “that lift was quantised!”. 

In 1987 he gave the [[Royal Institution Christmas Lectures]] on television. He was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in 1999<ref name=RSC/><ref name=whoswho/> and [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the 2012 New Year Honours for services to chemistry.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=60009 |date=31 December 2011 |page=8 |supp=y}}</ref> In May 2011 he was the guest on [[Desert Island Discs]]<ref name=Desert/> and in June 2012 was [[Michael Berkeley]]'s guest on [[Private Passions]].{{citation needed|date=July 2015}}

===Views on nuclear power===
Ahead of the 50th anniversary of the 1962 James Bond film ''[[Dr. No (film)|Dr No]]'', Phillips stated that the character of Dr No, with his personal [[nuclear reactor]], helped to create a "remorselessly grim" reputation for atomic energy.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/education-16509668|work=[[BBC News]]|title=James Bond villains blamed for nuclear's bad image|date=12 January 2012|last1=Coughlan|first1=Sean}}</ref> and that the popularity of the movie created an enduringly negative image of [[nuclear power]] – as something dangerous that could be wielded by megalomaniacs with aspirations to world domination. Phillips claims that when nuclear power is discussed "it is not at all surprising that the public at home and abroad are sceptical" and concludes that "The [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] asserts that nuclear power has to be part of the future national [[energy mix]], in which it plays a major role. [[Fossil fuel]]s have to be eradicated for people to live in a healthy environment. Let's say yes to nuclear and no to Dr No's nonsense."

==Awards and honours==
Phillips received the Porter Medal in 2010<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/88924/emeritus-professor-david-phillips-obe-awarded/ | title=Emeritus Professor David Phillips OBE awarded the Porter Medal &#124; Imperial News &#124; Imperial College London | date=30 April 2010 }}</ref> and was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2015|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2015]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117101307/https://royalsociety.org/people/david-phillips-12094/|archive-date=2015-11-17|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/david-phillips-12094/|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|title=Professor David Phillips CBE FRS}}</ref>
